e-568.knowledge_point: Finding the Total Displacement of a Particle Given Its Velocity
e-568.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t$ is given by $v(t) = 2t + 3t^2.$ What is the total displacement of the particle between $t=1$ and $t=3?$
e-568.worked_solution:
We find the total displacement by calculating the definite integral of the velocity.

Let $d$ be the total displacement. Then, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={\int }_{1}^{3}(2t+3{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={({t}^{2}+{t}^{3})|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =[{3}^{2}+{3}^{3}]-[{1}^{2}+{1}^{3}] \\  & =[9+27]-[1+1] \\  & =36-2 \\  & =34.\end{aligned}
$$

So the total displacement between $t=1$ and $t=3$ is $34.$

e-7128.knowledge_point: Finding the Final Position of a Particle
e-7128.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t) = 6t^2 +4t.$ At time $t=2$ the particle is located at the position $x=-20.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=4?$
e-7128.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=4$ is equal to its position at $t=2$ plus the total displacement over $t\in[2,4].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(4) = x(2) + \int_2^4 v(t)\,\textrm{d}t
$$

Carrying out the computations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(4) & =-20+{\int }_{2}^{4}(6{t}^{2}+4t)\,\text{dt} \\  & =-20+{[2{t}^{3}+2{t}^{2}]}_{2}^{4} \\  & =-20+([2(4)^{3}+2(4)^{2}]-[2(2)^{3}+2(2)^{2}]) \\  & =-20+([128+32]-[16+8]) \\  & =-20+(160-24) \\  & =-20+136 \\  & =116.\end{aligned}
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=4$ is $x=116.$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=3{t}^{2}-4t.$ What is the total displacement of the particle between $t=2$ and $t=4?$
after.worked_solution:
We find the total displacement by calculating the definite integral of the velocity.

Let $d$ be the total displacement. Then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={\int }_{2}^{4}(3{t}^{2}-4t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={({t}^{3}-2{t}^{2})|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =[(4)^{3}-2(4)^{2}]-[(2)^{3}-2(2)^{2}] \\  & =[64-32]-[8-8] \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

So the total displacement between $t=2$ and $t=4$ is $32.$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Final Position of a Particle
content.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=2t+{t}^{2}.$ At time $t=1$ the particle is located at the position $x=4.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=3?$
content.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=3$ is equal to its position at $t=1$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [1,3].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(3)=x(1)+{\int }_{1}^{3}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Carrying out the computations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(3) & =4+{\int }_{1}^{3}(2t+{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =4+{[{t}^{2}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =4+([{3}^{2}+\frac{{3}^{3}}{3}]-[{1}^{2}+\frac{{1}^{3}}{3}]) \\  & =4+([9+9]-[1+\frac{1}{3}]) \\  & =4+(18-\frac{4}{3}) \\  & =4+\frac{50}{3} \\  & =\frac{62}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=3$ is $x=\frac{62}{3}.$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(2) & =e+{\int }_{1}^{2}{e}^{2-t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =e+{[-{e}^{2-t}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =e+([-{e}^{2-2}]-[-{e}^{2-1}]) \\  & =e+([-{e}^{0}]-[-{e}^{1}]) \\  & =e+(-1+e) \\  & =2e-1\end{aligned}
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=2$ is $x=2e-1.$
